name: Carrow Dockside Denim Jacket
description:
A heavy-weight raw denim jacket in indigo-black, cut boxy and generous through the shoulders with reinforced elbows and a double-button chest. The fabric is stiff when new and softens into creases unique to each wearer over months of use. Contrast stitching in burnt orange runs along the seams. Four exterior pockets, all with button closures. The collar is unlined and slightly oversized — good for turning up against lake wind.

Carrow is a Tier 2 street label out of the old Pilsen manufacturing district. No tech, no gimmicks. Workers, students, and anyone who appreciates something that lasts wear this jacket until it falls apart, then wear it a little longer.
what_it_says: You work hard and you don't need to announce it. You've had this jacket for three years and plan to have it for ten more.
worn_by: Shelf climbers who made it to Tier 2
story_hooks: A serial number stamped inside the collar traces back to a Carrow run that was supposedly destroyed — the batch linked to a labor dispute three years ago
The previous owner's name is written in marker on the inner chest pocket, and that person is now missing
A fence at the Pilsen market is offering these at half price, no questions asked — too many of them, all the same size
